answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a time-delayed bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. Reputation and access accrue to the bonded key over repeated, auditable transactions, while disputed work can slash the bond after review. Creating a hundred identities therefore means buying and immobilizing a hundred bonds, not merely generating keys; the attacker pays capital costs and risks losing it. Rotating labels such as cedar, walnut, or comet does not evade the requirement.
